title: Two exact quantum queries use at most six variables
abstract: We give a direct analytic proof that every total Boolean function computable exactly with at most two quantum queries depends on at most six input variables. This bound is sharp. A previous derivation relied on a numerical classification of Boolean functions on at most four variables; to the best of our knowledge, ours is the first unconditional proof. The main difficulty beyond the one-query case is that query-path vectors need not be mutually orthogonal, so interference prevents the scalar weight-counting argument from applying. We overcome this difficulty by establishing a rigid support-and-branch decomposition: after the coordinates in the first-query support are fixed, the second query induces a family of exact one-query branches. This structural description may be of independent interest.
summary: This paper analytically proves an upper bound on the number of variables needed for a Boolean function computable by only two quantum queries. It establishes that this number is at most six, providing a rigorous proof where previous methods relied on numerical classifications. The work advances the theoretical understanding of quantum query complexity by developing a novel structural decomposition technique.
main_problem: To provide a direct analytic proof bounding the number of input variables required for a total Boolean function computable exactly with at most two quantum queries.
main_result: The paper proves that every such function depends on at most six input variables, establishing the bound $	ext{JE}(2) \le 6$ with an unconditional proof.
method: The proof uses a structural decomposition of the two-query algorithm, overcoming the difficulty that query-path vectors are not necessarily mutually orthogonal, and bounding the variables based on the support of the first query.
model_or_system: The analysis concerns quantum query complexity ($	ext{QE}(F)$) for a total Boolean function $F: \{+1, -1\}^n 	o \{+1, -1\}$, modeled using query-path vectors and quantum state evolution.
key_observables: The number of relevant coordinates ($	ext{rv}(F)$) and the quantum query complexity ($	ext{QE}(F)$).
important_parameters: The number of queries ($k=2$), the size of the first-query support ($|S|$), and the structure of the resulting one-query branches.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of an exact two-query quantum algorithm for the function $F$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from analyzing the one-query case (relying on orthogonality) to establishing structural properties of the two-query state. It proceeds by bounding the support size ($|S|$) based on the number of relevant variables ($	ext{rv}(F)$) and then using the structure of the resulting one-query branches to derive the final upper bound.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical techniques developed for bounding query complexity, especially the structural decomposition, are highly relevant to understanding the limitations and computational power of quantum algorithms in general.
